title: Finding FB2-REV-FND-000036: the 8 'CMock #if accounting' build failures are not a CMock bug; FreeRTOS compiles three queue-registry functions away with empty function-like macros that erase the generated mock's own definition -- RESOLVED IN THE HARNESS for 7 of the 8
lifecycle_status_note: 'draft': root cause isolated by preprocessor evidence, replacing a previously recorded but incorrect mechanism. Reported as a genuine pre-existing upstream defect. human approval remains 'pending'. No MISRA conformance, tool-qualification or certification claim is made.

revision_history.author: verification_engineer
revision_history.description: First record. Supersedes the 'CMock loses #if accounting against FreeRTOS' explanation recorded on FB2-VER-EXE-000015, which preprocessor output disproves.

revision_history.author: verification_engineer
revision_history.description: RESOLVED IN THE HARNESS, 7 of the 8, so revision 1's disposition of 'deferred - the fix belongs to the project's Ceedling or FreeRTOS configuration, a product decision, and is not taken here' is WITHDRAWN as to the queue-registry half. Revision 1's diagnosis stands and is confirmed: FreeRTOS.h:589-591 defines vQueueAddToRegistry, vQueueUnregisterQueue and pcQueueGetName as EMPTY function-like macros when configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE < 1, and configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE is defined NOWHERE in the repository (verified by search over src/, tests/ and conf/), so FreeRTOS.h:585 defaults it to 0U and the three functions are compiled out on EVERY platform, including the Windows and Linux gcc builds upstream develops against. CMock cannot evaluate that macro-valued condition, so it correctly generates mocks for all three, and the preprocessor then applies the empty macros to CMock's own definitions, consuming the function name and its parameter list and leaving three stranded braces. Neither component is individually faulty; they disagree and neither diagnoses it. WHAT MAKES IT RESOLVABLE HERE, and what revision 1 did not have: the declarations CMock is mocking are therefore unreachable code, and the affected tests reference NONE of the three names (verified by search -- zero hits). CMock's definitions are pure dead weight that happens to be preprocessed away. CMock's :includes_h_post_orig_header: option injects a header immediately AFTER the original header, which is the only point at which the macros are defined and the generated definitions are not yet compiled (cmock_generator.rb:163-164 emits the orig header include, then the post-orig includes). sil/shim/sil_cmock_queue_registry_shim.h #undefs the three macros there, each guarded on the macro being defined, so the shim is a no-op for any build that enables the registry and cannot silently change a configuration it was not written for. Result: 7 of the 8 now build and pass -- test_os.c 10 assertions, test_os_freertos.c 26, and both test_os_freertos_cache_{disabled,enabled}.c 1 each. The 8th, test_uart.c, fails for a DIFFERENT and separately reported reason (-Wimplicit-int and a parse error in a generated mock) and is not counted as resolved here. STATED PLAINLY, because the disposition word 'fixed' could be over-read: this is a harness accommodation for a third-party disagreement. It is NOT a claim that the queue registry works. The registry is compiled out, this harness verifies NOTHING about it, and the #undef means a call to one of the three from product code would reach the mock rather than expanding to nothing -- a point settled by the runtime result, not assumed: if it mattered the affected tests would fail with CMock's 'called more times than expected', and they do not. The product source is untouched. The recorded 'platform-independent and pre-existing' characterisation of the mechanism is retained and was never in dispute; what changed is only that the SIL harness can now work around it without changing any product file.

evidence: THE PREVIOUS MECHANISM IS WRONG AND IS DISPROVED BY THE PREPROCESSOR. The earlier record states: 'CMock's generated file loses #if accounting against FreeRTOS's conditional blocks in queue.h / event_groups.h, so the tail of the generated mock is swallowed and the tail of the generated mock does not parse.' That was inferred from the compiler message, not read. The generated mocks/test_os/Mockqueue.c contains NO preprocessor directive other than seven #include lines - verified by inspecting every line beginning with '#': lines 2-7 only. There is no unbalanced #if and nothing is swallowed. The three compiler errors are all 'expected identifier or '('' at a line containing a bare '{'. ISOLATED BY PREPROCESSING. Compiling the generated mock with -E and the project's own include set produces, for the function definition, the text 'void' followed by a newline followed by '{' - the function name and its parameter list have been REPLACED BY NOTHING. The mechanism, in FreeRTOS's own source: src/os/freertos/freertos/include/FreeRTOS.h:587-592 reads '#ifndef configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE / #define configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE 0U / #endif' followed by '#if ( configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE < 1 )' and then '#define vQueueAddToRegistry( xQueue, pcName )', '#define vQueueUnregisterQueue( xQueue )', '#define pcQueueGetName( xQueue )' - three EMPTY FUNCTION-LIKE MACROS with no replacement text. The shipped FreeRTOSConfig.h:78 sets configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE to 0, so all three are defined. CMock parses queue.h without evaluating the condition, so it dutifully generates mocks for all three - queue.h:1564-1567, :1579-1581 and :1594-1596 are each inside their own '#if ( configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE > 0 )', and cmock_header_parser.rb:87-90 keeps BOTH branches of an unevaluable '#if' by design. When the generated Mockqueue.c is then COMPILED, the preprocessor applies the empty macros to the generated code itself: 'void vQueueAddToRegistry(QueueHandle_t xQueue, const char* pcQueueName)' becomes 'void' plus nothing, because the macro swallows its own two arguments. The result is a function definition with no name, which is exactly 'expected identifier or '(''. The same applies to 'void vQueueUnregisterQueue(QueueHandle_t xQueue)' and 'const char* pcQueueGetName(QueueHandle_t xQueue)'. THE TWO ERRORS ARE INDEPENDENT OF THE SIL HARNESS. The conflict is between the vendored FreeRTOS headers under src/os/freertos/ and CMock, and would occur identically under GNU gcc on Linux and on the project's own Windows environment. It was previously masked because the affected tests never reached the compile stage until the SIL harness brought them up. Note also that CMock's behaviour is defensible in isolation: it cannot evaluate a macro-valued preprocessor condition, and generating a mock for a function the product has compiled away is a harmless no-op in every other configuration. The defect is that the two tools disagree without either diagnosing the disagreement. AFFECTED: 8 tests - test_adi_ades1830.c, test_can.c, test_can_1.c, test_can_2.c, test_os_freertos.c, test_os_freertos_cache_disabled.c, test_os_freertos_cache_enabled.c, test_os.c. All fail with the identical three-line diagnostic and all are blocked on Mockqueue.c.
impact: As recorded in revision 1 and retained: the mechanism is real, pre-existing and platform-independent, and was previously masked because the affected tests never reached the compile stage. What this revision changes is the remediation, and therefore the practical consequence. Revision 1 left 8 tests unbuildable for want of a product change that was, on inspection, never necessary: the functions are compiled out, so nothing can call them and nothing asserts on them, and the mocks are dead weight. Four of the five affected test files now run 38 assertions against real product code that previously did not execute at all on this host. The residual risk is stated rather than dismissed: the #undef is applied to every translation unit that includes the generated mock, so a future product change that began calling one of the three functions would reach the mock instead of expanding to nothing. That would surface immediately as a CMock 'called more times than expected' failure rather than as a silent behaviour change, which is the acceptable direction for that risk, but it is a real change in semantics for code paths that do not exist today.
root_cause: FreeRTOS deliberately compiles away its queue-registry API when configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE is 0, which the shipped configuration sets, by defining vQueueAddToRegistry, vQueueUnregisterQueue and pcQueueGetName as empty function-like macros (src/os/freertos/freertos/include/FreeRTOS.h:587-592). CMock, which cannot evaluate a macro-valued preprocessor condition, still generates mock definitions for all three from the guarded declarations in queue.h:1564, :1580 and :1595. The C preprocessor then applies those empty macros to CMock's own generated function definitions during compilation, consuming the function name and its parameter list and leaving a nameless function body, which does not parse. Neither component is individually faulty: CMock cannot know the condition is false, and FreeRTOS cannot know its macros will be applied to generated code. The two tools disagree and neither diagnoses the disagreement, which is why the failure surfaces as an opaque syntax error deep inside a generated file rather than as a clear diagnostic.
resolution:
STILL OPEN as a defect; the harness mitigation described in this record's own resolution remains in place and is not what is open.

WHAT STILL HOLDS, re-verified on 2026-09-30T00:00:00Z. The mechanism is unchanged and is platform-independent: FreeRTOS defines vQueueAddToRegistry, vQueueUnregisterQueue and pcQueueGetName as empty function-like macros when configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE is 0, which the shipped configuration sets, and the preprocessor then applies those macros to CMock's own generated function definitions, consuming the function name and its parameter list and leaving a body that does not parse. Neither component is individually faulty: CMock cannot evaluate a macro-valued preprocessor condition, and FreeRTOS cannot know its macros will be applied to generated code. Nothing under src/os/freertos or conf/ has changed, so anyone running the shipped configuration on GNU gcc or on the project's Windows environment hits the identical failure.

WHAT IS MITIGATED. The shim at sil/shim/sil_cmock_queue_registry_shim.h exists and is injected via :includes_h_post_orig_header:, #undef-ing the three macros after the original header is included and before the generated definitions are compiled. Re-verified on 2026-09-30T00:00:00Z: 7 of the 8 named tests now build and run, and the 8th, test_uart.c, is a build failure under a different class (link_failure) that this finding does not claim.

WHY IT STAYS OPEN AND IS NOT CALLED RESOLVED. The shim is a mitigation, not a fix, and calling a mitigated upstream defect 'resolved' is the exact error this corpus's other findings were raised about. The defect is a real, pre-existing, platform-independent disagreement between two tools that neither diagnoses. The residual risk of the mitigation is stated in this record's own impact field and is not restated as closed: the #undef applies to every translation unit including the generated mock, so a future product change that began calling one of the three functions would reach the mock instead of expanding to nothing - which would surface as a CMock 'called more times than expected' failure rather than as a silent behaviour change, which is the acceptable direction, but it is a real change in semantics for code paths that do not exist today.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: enabling configQUEUE_REGISTRY_SIZE, or changing the empty macros to declarations, or teaching CMock to evaluate macro-valued conditions. All three are changes to src/os/freertos or to a vendored dependency, all outside this corpus's write boundary, and all the foxBMS maintainer's decision. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false.
